3.13.1.1–7. Section on Dependent Origination, etc. (Paṭiccādivāra).
The Tetrad of Conditions:
Dependent upon a wholesome state that is to be abandoned by insight, there arises a wholesome state that is to be abandoned by insight, by way of root condition. (Abbreviated.)
With respect to root condition: one; with respect to object condition: one; with respect to predominance condition: one … pe … with respect to non-disappearance condition: one.
Dependent on unwholesome states that are to be abandoned by vision, there arises an unwholesome state to be abandoned by vision by way of root condition.

(Abbreviated. With respect to root condition: two; with respect to object condition: two; with respect to predominance condition: two … pe … with respect to non-disappearance condition: two. (Abbreviated.)

Dependent on unwholesome states abandonable by vision (*dassanena pahātabba*), an unwholesome state abandonable by vision arises by way of the not-root condition (*na-hetupaccaya*): dependent on the aggregates associated with doubt (*vicikicchā-sahagata*), doubt-associated delusion (*moha*) arises.

Dependent on unwholesome states not abandonable by vision, an unwholesome state not abandonable by vision arises by way of the not-root condition. (Abbreviated. In the "not-root" [section] there are two; in the "not-predominance" (*na-adhipati*) [section], two;

in the "not-prenascence" (*na-purejāta*) [section], two... [and so on] ...in the "not-kamma" (*na-kamma*) [section], two; in the "not-resultant" (*na-vipāka*) [section], two; in the "not-dissociation" (*na-vippayutta*) [section], two.
An unwholesome state to be abandoned by seeing is a condition, as a root-condition, for an unwholesome state to be abandoned by seeing.
An unwholesome state not to be abandoned by seeing is a condition, as a root-condition, for an unwholesome state not to be abandoned by seeing. (Abbreviated.
There are two [conditions] under root; three under object (one under seeing, two under non-seeing); three under predominance (under seeing...).

One [condition] based on what is to be abandoned (*pahātabba*); two based on non-seeing (*nadassana*): objective predominance (*ārammaṇādhipati*), co-nascent predominance (*sahajātādhipati*), and single-object predominance (*ekārammaṇādhipati*);

two in the immediate condition (*anantara*): one based on seeing and one not based on seeing; two in the contiguity condition (*samanantara*); two in the co-nascence condition (*sahajāta*) ... pe ... three in the decisive support condition (*upanissaya*);

two in the repetition condition (*āsevana*); two in the kamma condition (*kamma*); two in the nutriment condition (*āhāra*) ... pe ... two in the association condition (*sampayutta*); [two] in the presence condition (*atthi*).
Two for non-existence, two for absence … [and so on] … two for non-disappearance. (Abbreviated.
Dependent on an indeterminate state not to be abandoned by vision, an indeterminate state not to be abandoned by vision arises by way of root-condition. (Abbreviated.
One for root, one for object … [and so on] … one for non-disappearance. (Abbreviated.)
(In the section on co-arising, ...pe... and in the section on questions, it is one in all cases. 3.13.2.
The Dyad on What is to be Abandoned by Development, The Triplet on the Wholesome.
3.13.2.1–7. The Section on Dependent, etc. (Paṭiccādivāra)
The Tetrad of Conditions:
Dependent on a wholesome state not to be abandoned by cultivation, a wholesome state not to be abandoned by cultivation arises by way of root-condition. (Abbreviated.
Under root there is one; under object there is one … pe … under non-disappearance there is one. (Abbreviated.)
(In the section on co-nascence as well... [and so on] ...in the section on inquiry as well, it is one in all cases.
Dependent on an unwholesome state that is to be abandoned by cultivation, an unwholesome state that is to be abandoned by cultivation arises by way of root condition. (Abbreviated.
There are two under root, two under object... [and so on] ...two under non-disappearance.
Dependent on an indeterminate state not to be abandoned by cultivation, there arises an indeterminate state not to be abandoned by cultivation by way of root-condition.
(Abbreviated. Under root-condition: one; under object-condition: one … pe … under non-disappearance-condition: one. (Abbreviated.
[The same applies] in the section on conascence … and in the section on inquiry, in all cases: one.
3.13.3. The Dyad on Roots to be Abandoned by Seeing; The Triplet on the Wholesome (Kusalattika) 3.13.3.1–7. The Section on “Dependent Upon” Etc.;
The Tetrad on Conditions (Paccayacatukka).
Dependent on a wholesome state whose root is to be abandoned by insight, there arises a wholesome state whose root is to be abandoned by insight, by way of root-condition. (Abbreviated.
Under root-condition there is one; under object-condition there is one … pe … under non-disappearance-condition there is one. (Abbreviated.
(In the “Conascent” section … pe … and in the “Investigation” section, there is one in every instance.)
Dependent on an unwholesome state whose root is to be abandoned by vision, an unwholesome state whose root is to be abandoned by vision arises by way of the root condition.

Dependent on an unwholesome state whose root is not to be abandoned by vision, an unwholesome state whose root is not to be abandoned by vision arises by way of the root condition. [Dependent on] an unwholesome state whose root is not to be abandoned by vision...
Dependent on [a state] rooted in what is to be abandoned by seeing, an unwholesome state rooted in what is to be abandoned by seeing arises by way of root-condition (*hetu-paccaya*).

Dependent on both an unwholesome state rooted in what is to be abandoned by seeing and an unwholesome state not rooted in what is to be abandoned by seeing, an unwholesome state rooted in what is to be abandoned by seeing arises by way of root-condition.

Dependent on an unwholesome state rooted in what is to be abandoned by seeing, an unwholesome state rooted in what is to be abandoned by seeing arises by way of object-condition (*ārammaṇa-paccaya*)—three [cases]. (Two for "not by seeing," one for "conjunction"; abbreviated.)
In the case of root condition: four; object condition: six; predominance condition: two (six in all cases); non-disappearance condition: six. (Abbreviated.
Dependent on an unwholesome state rooted in a cause to be abandoned by vision, an unwholesome state not rooted in a cause to be abandoned by vision arises by way of the root condition.

Dependent on an unwholesome state not rooted in a cause to be abandoned by vision, an unwholesome state not rooted in a cause to be abandoned by vision arises by way of the root condition. (Abbreviated.)
With not-root condition: two; with not-predominance condition: six ... pe ... with not-kamma condition: four; with not-resultant condition: six; with not-dissociation condition: six.
An unwholesome state rooted in what is to be abandoned by seeing is a condition, by way of root-condition, for an unwholesome state rooted in what is to be abandoned by seeing.
(Abbreviated. With root condition: three; with object condition: nine; with predominance condition: three (one for seeing, two for non-seeing); with proximity condition: [nine].

Nine [conditions] by way of proximity; nine by way of contiguity; six by way of co-nascence … pe … nine by way of decisive support; nine by way of repetition; four by way of kamma; four by way of nutriment;
four by way of faculty … pe … six by way of association; six by way of presence; nine by way of absence … pe … six by way of non-disappearance. (Abbreviated.)
Dependent on an indeterminate state whose root is to be abandoned by insight, there arises an indeterminate state whose root is to be abandoned by insight, by way of root-condition.
(Abbreviated. Under root-condition: one; under object-condition: one … pe … under non-disappearance-condition: one. (Abbreviated.
[The same applies] in the section on co-nascence … pe … and in the section on inquiry, in all cases: one.
3.13.4. The Dyad on Roots to be Abandoned by Cultivation (Bhāvanāya-pahātabba-hetuka-duka), within the Wholesome Triad (Kusalattika) 3.13.4.1–7.
The Section on Dependent Origination, etc. (Paṭicca-ādi-vāra):
The Tetrad of Conditions (Paccaya-catukka).

Dependent on a wholesome state whose root is not to be abandoned by cultivation, there arises a wholesome state whose root is not to be abandoned by cultivation, by way of root-condition. (Abbreviated.
Under root-condition there is one; under object-condition there is one … pe … under non-disappearance-condition there is one. (Abbreviated.
(In the section on co-nascence … pe … and in the section on inquiry, there is one in every instance.)

Dependent on an unwholesome state whose root is to be abandoned by cultivation (*bhāvanāya pahātabbahetuka*), an unwholesome state whose root is to be abandoned by cultivation arises by way of the root condition (*hetupaccaya*).

Dependent on an unwholesome state whose root is not to be abandoned by cultivation (*nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetuka*), an unwholesome state whose root is not to be abandoned by cultivation arises by way of the root condition. ... three. (Abbreviated. Under the root [condition] there are four;
under the object [condition], six; under the predominance [condition], two ... pe ... under non-disappearance [condition], six.
Dependent on an indeterminate state whose root is not to be abandoned by cultivation, there arises an indeterminate state whose root is not to be abandoned by cultivation, by way of root-condition.
(Abbreviated. Under root-condition: one; under object-condition: one … pe … under non-disappearance-condition: one. (Abbreviated.
[The same applies] in the section on co-nascence … and in the section on inquiry, in all cases: one.
3.13.5. The Dyad of With-Initial-Application (Savitakkaduka), within the Triplet of the Wholesome (Kusalattika) 3.13.5.1.
The Section on the Wholesome (Kusalapada) 3.13.5.1.1–6.
The Chapter on "Dependent upon" and so forth (Paṭiccādivāra)
The Tetrad of Conditions:
Dependent on a wholesome state accompanied by initial application (*savitakka*), a wholesome state accompanied by initial application arises by way of root condition (*hetupaccaya*).
Dependent on a wholesome state accompanied by initial application, a wholesome state unaccompanied by initial application (*avitakka*) arises by way of root condition.

Dependent on a wholesome state accompanied by applied thought (*savitakka*), wholesome states both accompanied by applied thought and free from applied thought (*avitakka*) arise by way of root condition (*hetupaccaya*).

Dependent on a wholesome state free from applied thought, a wholesome state free from applied thought arises by way of root condition. Dependent on a wholesome state free from applied thought, a wholesome state accompanied by applied thought arises by way of root condition.

Dependent on wholesome states with applied thought (*savitakka*) and wholesome states without applied thought (*avitakka*), a wholesome state with applied thought arises by way of root condition. (Abbreviated.
There are six for root, six for object (six in all cases), and six for non-disappearance. (Abbreviated.
There are six for non-predominance, six for non-prenascence …pe… four for non-kamma …pe… six for non-dissociation. (Abbreviated.)
(The Chapter on Co-nascence ... and the Chapter on Association should also be expanded in detail. 3.13.5.1.7.
Chapter of Questions:
The Tetrad on Conditions.
Root-object condition: A wholesome state accompanied by applied thought (*savitakka*) is a condition, by way of root-condition (*hetupaccaya*), for a wholesome state accompanied by applied thought.

A wholesome state accompanied by applied thought is a condition, by way of root-condition, for a wholesome state unaccompanied by applied thought (*avitakka*). A wholesome state accompanied by applied thought...

A state accompanied by applied thought (*savitakka*) that is wholesome is a condition, by way of the root-condition (*hetu-paccaya*), for a state that is wholesome and either with or without applied thought.
A wholesome state without applied thought (*avitakka*) is a condition, by way of the root-condition, for a wholesome state without applied thought.
A wholesome state accompanied by applied thought is a condition, by way of the object-condition (*ārammaṇa-paccaya*), for a wholesome state accompanied by applied thought—three [instances].
A wholesome state without applied thought (*avitakka*) is a condition for a wholesome state without applied thought by way of object-condition (*ārammaṇapaccaya*)—three [instances].

Wholesome states with applied thought (*savitakka*) and wholesome states without applied thought are conditions for a wholesome state with applied thought by way of object-condition—three [instances].

(Abbreviated. Under root-cause (*hetu*), there are four; under object, nine; under predominance (*adhipati*), nine (in the three [preceding cases], co-nascent predominance [is included]; in the case without applied thought...).
One (conascence-predominance), nine in the immediate, nine in the contiguity, six in the conascence ... [etc.

... nine in the decisive support, nine in the repetition, four in kamma, four in nutriment, four in faculty, six in jhāna, six in the path, six in association, six in presence, nine in absence, nine in disappearance, six in non-disappearance. (Abbreviated.)
In the absence of the root condition, nine; in the absence of the object condition, nine. (Abbreviated.
With the root condition, in the absence of the object condition, four. (Abbreviated.
In the absence of the root condition, in the presence of the object condition, nine. (Abbreviated.)
(As in the section on questions in the *Kusalattika*, so it should be expanded in detail.
3.13.5.2. Unwholesome Section:
Dependent upon a wholesome-with-applied-thought unwholesome state, a wholesome-with-applied-thought unwholesome state arises by way of root condition.
Dependent on an unwholesome state accompanied by applied thought (*savitakka*), an unwholesome state without applied thought (*avitakka*) arises by way of root condition (*hetupaccaya*).
Dependent on an unwholesome state accompanied by applied thought, both unwholesome states— those with applied thought and those without applied thought—
arise by way of root condition.
Dependent on an unwholesome state without applied thought (*avitakka*), an unwholesome state with applied thought (*savitakka*) arises by way of root condition (*hetupaccaya*).
Dependent on both an unwholesome state with applied thought and an unwholesome state without applied thought, an unwholesome state with applied thought arises by way of root condition. (Abbreviated.
Under root [condition] there are five; under object [condition] there are five (five in all cases) …pe… under non-disappearance [condition] there are five. (Abbreviated.)
Dependent on a wholesome state with applied thought, a wholesome state with applied thought arises by way of the not-root condition.
Dependent on a wholesome state without applied thought, a wholesome state with applied thought arises by way of the not-root condition.
Dependent on both a wholesome state with applied thought and a wholesome state without applied thought, a wholesome state with applied thought arises by way of the not-root condition. (Abbreviated.)
Three by way of not-root, five by way of not-predominance, three by way of not-kamma … pe … five by way of not-dissociation.
An unwholesome state accompanied by initial application is a condition, by way of root-condition, for an unwholesome state accompanied by initial application. (Abbreviated.
Three by way of root, nine by way of object, nine by way of predominance, nine by way of proximity … pe … five by way of conascence … pe …
In the case of decisive support, nine; in repetition, nine; in kamma, three; in nutriment, three … pe … in jhāna, five;
in the path, five; in association, five; in presence, five; in absence, nine … pe … in non-disappearance, five.
(Abbreviated. 3.13.5.3. The Indeterminate Section.
Dependent on a state with applied thought that is indeterminate, a state with applied thought that is indeterminate arises by way of root condition … three.
Dependent on a state without applied thought that is indeterminate, a state without applied thought that is indeterminate arises by way of root condition … three.
Dependent on a state both with and without applied thought that is indeterminate, a state with applied thought that is indeterminate arises by way of root condition … three. (Abbreviated.)

With respect to root-condition: nine; with respect to object-condition: nine ... pe ... with respect to prenascence and repetition-conditions: six ... pe ... with respect to non-disappearance-condition: nine. (Abbreviated. With respect to not-root: nine;
with respect to not-object: three; with respect to not-predominance: nine ... pe ... with respect to not-prenascence:

nine ... pe ... with respect to not-kamma: four; with respect to not-resultant: nine; with respect to not-nutriment: one; with respect to not-faculty: one; with respect to not-jhāna: one; with respect to not-path: nine.
With non-associated [condition], three; with non-dissociated, six …pe… with non-disappeared, three.
A determinate state accompanied by initial application (savitakka) is a condition, by way of root-condition (hetupaccaya), for a determinate state accompanied by initial application … three.
An indeterminate state without initial application (avitakka) is a condition, by way of root-condition, for an indeterminate state without initial application.
A state accompanied by applied thought and indeterminate is a condition, by way of object-condition, for a state accompanied by applied thought and indeterminate.
(Abbreviated. Under root: four; under object: nine; under predominance: nine (nine in all cases); under decisive support: nine; under prenascence:
three; under postnascence: three; under repetition: nine; under kamma: four; under result: nine; under nutriment: four.
…pe… nine in jhāna, nine in path, six in association, five in dissociation, nine in presence, nine in absence, nine in disappearance, nine in non-disappearance. (Abbreviated.
Nine in not-root, nine in not-object. (Abbreviated.)
With root condition, not-object: four. (Abbreviated.
With not-root condition, object: nine. (Abbreviated.

Dependent on a wholesome state with sustained thought, a wholesome state with sustained thought arises by way of root condition... three.
Dependent on a wholesome state without sustained thought, a wholesome state without sustained thought arises by way of root condition... two.
Dependent on both a wholesome state with sustained thought and a wholesome state without sustained thought, a wholesome state with sustained thought arises by way of root condition. (Abbreviated.)
In the case of root condition, there are six; in the case of object condition, there are six ... pe ... in the case of non-disappearance condition, there are six.
Dependent on an unwholesome state accompanied by sustained thought (*savicāra*), an unwholesome state accompanied by sustained thought arises by way of root condition ... three.
Dependent on an unwholesome state not accompanied by sustained thought (*avicāra*), an unwholesome state accompanied by sustained thought arises by way of root condition.

Dependent on unwholesome states with sustained thought (*savicāra*) and unwholesome states without sustained thought (*avicāra*), an unwholesome state with sustained thought arises by way of the root condition (*hetu-paccaya*). (Abbreviated.
Five in the case of roots, five in the case of objects (*ārammaṇa*) … pe … five in the case of non-disappearance (*avigata*).
Dependent on indeterminate (*abyākata*) states with sustained thought, an indeterminate state with sustained thought arises by way of the root condition … three.

Dependent on a state that is without sustained thought (*avicāra*) and indeterminate (*abyākata*), there arises a state that is without sustained thought and indeterminate by way of root condition (*hetu-paccaya*) ... three.

Dependent on a state that is both with sustained thought (*savicāra*) and indeterminate, and a state that is without sustained thought and indeterminate, there arises a state that is with sustained thought and indeterminate by way of root condition ...
three. (Abbreviated. Nine for root; nine for object ... pe ... six for prenascence and repetition ... pe ... nine for result ... pe ... nine for non-disappearance.

A state with sustained thought that is indeterminate is a condition, by way of root-condition, for a state with sustained thought that is indeterminate. (Abbreviated. Under root-condition there are four;
under object-condition, nine ... pe ... under path-condition, four ... pe ... under non-disappearance-condition, nine. (Abbreviated.

With root condition, not-object: four. (Abbreviated.
With not-root condition, object: nine. (Abbreviated.

The Tetrad of Conditions:
Dependent upon a wholesome state accompanied by rapture, a wholesome state accompanied by rapture arises by way of root condition.
Dependent upon a wholesome state accompanied by rapture, a wholesome state unaccompanied by rapture arises by way of root condition.
Dependent on a wholesome state accompanied by rapture, both a wholesome state accompanied by rapture and a wholesome state unaccompanied by rapture arise by way of root condition.

Dependent on a wholesome state unaccompanied by rapture, a wholesome state unaccompanied by rapture arises by way of root condition. Dependent on a wholesome state unaccompanied by rapture, a wholesome state accompanied by rapture arises by way of root condition.
Dependent on wholesome states with rapture and wholesome states without rapture, a wholesome state with rapture arises by way of root condition. (Abbreviated.

three. (Abbreviated. Under root condition there are nine; under object condition there are nine... pe ... under prenascence condition there are six, under repetition condition there are six... pe ... under non-disappearance condition there are nine.

The Tetrad of Conditions:
Dependent on a wholesome state accompanied by rapture … [and so forth]. (The wholesome, unwholesome, and indeterminate states are similar to the "With-Rapture" dyad.
